geometry_edits.rationale: Transform the existing notch into a true courtyard-like subtraction to produce a more legible public void and support neighborhood-living ground threshold logic.
Open the void a bit more so it reads as a usable court rather than a small indentation.
Orient the open side toward the verified access frame to reinforce public threshold behavior.

graph_edits.rationale: Upgrade the current entry notch into a clearer public void/court so the street edge becomes legible and programmatically usable.
Increase the carved open ground to strengthen publicness without fragmenting the main mass.
Align the void to the verified access side so the frontage reads as an entry threshold rather than a sealed edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact block with a single dominant gesture and a visible carved ground response, but the massing remains fairly generic and the section does not strongly communicate neighborhood-living program through an active public threshold plus usable void. Across the four views it is mostly consistent, with no obvious view-to-view collision, so repair integrity is decent. The blue access edge is acknowledged by a notch/void, but the response is modest and not yet emphatically public. The silhouette is slightly stepped/chamfered without becoming a true inhabited terrace or a more convincing court-and-connector composition. Overall it is program-plausible but not fully program-fit enough for a hard pass because the public edge and section logic are underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a low-rise pavilion/community-center language; transfer the courtyard-and-bridge logic, not the curvilinear roof expression.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central void and an upper connector can create a clear public threshold while keeping the main body compact.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Bigger campus-like complexity; candidate should not over-fragment into multiple disconnected bars.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a large central void can support neighborhood-scale mixed program with legible hierarchy and terraces.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story pavilion logic is much smaller and flatter than the candidate’s mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple rectilinear base with a clear entry canopy/setback can establish a legible public ground edge for neighborhood commercial use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: residential waterfront slab/courtyard typology; useful only as a section/void principle, not as a direct form model.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped massing can work when the section is clearly inhabited and the void is spatially productive.

warnings: Parcel containment was not explicitly verifiable from the provided summary alone; if the green boundary is tight, recheck containment against all views.
The access response is present but semantically weak relative to the verified frontage; it should read more as a public threshold or court opening.
Avoid pushing this into a stair-like roof vocabulary; the program wants an active ground edge and usable void, not decorative stepping.
